title: Before the login
question: How early could an attacker get control of a website?
answer: Before the website’s own login code started.
explanation: PHP is software that builds web pages on a server, the computer that sends pages to your browser. In an attack demonstrated against Apache using mod_php, researchers made PHP run their instructions before the website checked a password. Running out of memory could interrupt setup. During cleanup, PHP could use unfinished data to decide which instructions ran next; researchers exploited that mistake to run their own. PHP released fixes on October 21, 2026. Email-alias service addy.io paused its website and web app while patching; email delivery continued.
qualification: The demonstration used Apache with mod_php, one way to run PHP. The attacker had the same permissions as the server program handling the request. That did not automatically give them control of the whole computer. Other PHP setups have different attack conditions. A demonstrated attack does not mean every affected website was hacked.
whyCare: Your login is one piece of a much larger system.

evidence.dataAsOf: October 21, 2026 security disclosure and operator report
evidence.denominator: No prevalence estimate or derived statistic. Server setup matters; a severity score is not a probability. No counts of hacked sites inferred.
evidence.methodology: PHP’s maintainers report a demonstrated attack against Apache with mod_php before website code runs. The out-of-memory advisory says failed allocation can leave partly initialized memory reachable and that shutdown can read or branch on it. The plain-language explanation describes that branching as using unfinished data to decide which instructions run next; the advisory separately confirms attacker-selected code running with the web worker account’s permissions. No specific pointer overwrite or claim that raw data becomes instructions is inferred. The separate stale-state flaw is not part of this illustration. Addy.io’s operator reports pausing its web services while patching, with email delivery continuing. Astra rechecked the PHP announcement, both advisories and Foundation account on October 21; the existing Foundation/GHSA disagreement about the OOM FPM demonstration remains outside the narrow mod_php claim. No exploit was run. Recheck current advisories before release.
